description: Ember Watch is a multipurpose, interactive platform which studies microgravity combustion and fire safety solutions. With its very own microgravity combustion modelling lab, users get to explore the physics and decision analysis of each unique case. Ember Watch features scientific analysis, summary and ranking of real NASA data, backed by meticulous proving and calculation.
summary:
Ember Watch is an AI powered super intelligent fire safety engine. It features a physics based simulator trained on real NASA data to predict the potential risk of microgravity combustion. It conducts meticulous analysis to provide practical advice on how to mitigate and manage the risk factors to prevent such catastrophe. 

With the recent uprise in space exploration trips, it is crucial for scientists and engineers to ensure the safety of our astronauts so that they may return home safely. As it stands, it is difficult for engineers to crunch the data and provide mitigation steps in time, as there are physical factors to take into consideration when providing a risk evaluation for microgravity combustion. Ember Watch is designed to help out with the computation using data provided by the user to ensure that the best help can be provided in time for our astronauts.
details:
Ember Watch

Key feature

Guided Tutorial

  • Introduces users to the platform's main features and how to use them.

Dashboard

  • Interactive 3D flame visualization using WebGL.
  • Fire-risk overview and monitoring.

Modeling Lab

  • Simulates fire risks under different cabin conditions.
  • Adjustable oxygen, airflow, cabin volume, fuel load and crew distance.
  • Dynamic risk scoring and interactive charts.

Methodology

  • Explains risk calculation formulas and scientific foundations.
  • Oxygen partial pressure calculations.
  • Evidence mapping and safety thresholds.

Safety Management

  • Historical spaceflight fire incident lessons.
  • Safety tracker for corrective actions, hazards and inspections.

References

  • NASA, JPL and NASA Spinoff research sources.
  • Nine NASA Excel datasets.
  • Traceable research references and source limitations.

How does it work?

Ember Watch forms effective decisions and detailed reports based on a Safety Decision Tree that we trained it on. Through which, it performs a detailed analysis on each step, and evaluates how the weight of the risk that is being studied. 

Ember Watch starts by continuously monitoring the spacecraft through sensor channels. Then, it processes these datas and performs its own analysis and interpretation of it based on previous real NASA data that we have trained it on. If the data collected indicates a potential risk, the model will proceed down the flow of the decision tree. If the data collected doesn't flag all of the requirements needed for it to be considered as a real safety risk, the SI will return to its initial state and perform continuous monitoring.

Continuing down the decision tree, Ember Watch proceeds to evaluate the fire characteristics and context based on the data it has collected, and predicts the risk level based on the individual weighted risk points of each set of data it has collected. Temperature, atmosphere, flame size all carry different sets of weighted risk points depending on their contribution towards microgravity combustion. A detailed risk report is then produced within seconds, that alerts engineers in real time and provides procedures and actions that need to be taken to mitigate the risk. Once the risk is mitigated, the incident will be logged and Ember Watch will perform its own internal data analysis, and from there, improve the system to provide even more accurate forecasts and improved risk reports in the future. 

Also building upon the decision tree, Ember Watch emphasizes on the fire safety insights by offering an integrated corrective action and inspection tracker. This feature ultimately allows the engineers to be aware of the actions assigned through the checklist method. Every assignment, whether completed or not, is able to be recorded and tracked through Ember Watch. It is also able to estimate the risk level during an emergency through the modelling lab based on the cabin layout submitted by engineers. Ember Watch provides a variety of past incident cases that possess valuable insights. Every case marks its own vital lessons and respective corrective actions for tracking purposes.

What benefits and impacts does it bring?

It is able to provide effective practical advice based on the situation and data provided, alongside a detailed risk report on several areas that may be of high risk, and thus allows the user to identify and take actions to reduce the risk of casualties during the astronaut’s mission. Built on real data and thousands of simulations, it acts as your personal advisor and provides a direction for when the situation involves many physical factors that change rapidly with time. In the event in which the AI model fails to accurately predict the outcome and provide practical risks, it’ll analyse its mistakes and remodel itself to adjust to new data, thus preventing errors like such to happen in the future. 

In terms of practical benefits, Ember Watch is capable of identifying what typical cameras miss, and what we as humans would’ve missed. Ember Watch is built on six sensor channels, covering various frequencies in the electromagnetic spectrum including notable frequencies that are associated with microgravity combustion such as infrared and UV frequencies. Invisible fires, are especially a huge risk during space missions, as we are unable to see it, astronauts in space will not be able to report it and by the time the we’ve detected the presence of invisible fires, the damages it has caused will be beyond irreparable and thus result in the termination of the mission. Ember Watch prevents this by alerting engineers and astronauts if a certain frequency is detected beyond its typical intensity, and offers mitigation steps to extinguish the invisible fire. 

Ember Watch brings substantial impact in manipulating the variables and uncertainties in space exploration missions. It allows engineers to track and control microgravity combustion, one of the most threatening factors in space missions. Ember Watch directs the future of human space exploration to a safer and more versatile position.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software are used in development of the project?

Backend:

  • Python (openpyxl) for NASA Excel data processing.
  • No database, server-side backend, or external AI/ML services.

Frontend:

  • HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript (Single-Page Application).
  • Chart.js 4.4.1, WebGL, custom GLSL shaders, inline SVG, and Google Fonts.

Data Sources:

  • Nine NASA Excel datasets.
  • NASA, JPL, and NASA Spinoff websites.

Deployment:

  • Claude Artifact tool for web hosting.
  • ZIP for packaging the editable source code.
  • Runs entirely in the browser.

Development Tools:

  • Claude Code (AI-assisted development).
  • Linux cloud sandbox.
  • Python, openpyxl, fontTools, Pillow.
  • Playwright and headless Chromium for automated testing.

Technical Stack

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS and Vanilla JavaScript.
  • Backend: No dedicated backend; entirely browser-based.
  • Data Sources: NASA, JPL and NASA Spinoff.
  • Data Storage: Browser localStorage (JSON).
  • Risk Engine: Deterministic calculations and predefined safety rules.
  • Graphics: WebGL, GLSL shaders, SVG and CSS.
  • Deployment: Vercel.

Future Improvements

  • AI-powered NASA research analysis.
  • Automatic floor plan recognition using computer vision.
  • Realistic evacuation pathfinding using A* algorithm.
  • AI-powered hazard classification.
  • Cloud database, user authentication and multi-user tracking.
